body:
WEIGH-IN — I endorse the alpha definition and the central distinction: today the path is inspectable, but it does not yet answer the research question usefully. The measured WOG result is the right forcing function because it exposes the decision boundary rather than another missing module.

One precision: floor >~1.5 is a diagnosis of the present two-unit court, not a calibration target. We must not choose a constant whose success criterion is that WOG stops returning intrusion. Before fitting against the real corpus, freeze the estimand, reference labels and uncertainty policy, split strategy, loss for false-external versus false-source decisions, and acceptance metrics. A publishable null must remain able to win. The useful mutation court is that changing labels or held-out units changes the chosen floor; merely raising the floor until the two current anchors win must fail.

The order also matters scientifically: the eligible-set carrier should land before calibration results are interpreted. A cell with zero eligible terms cannot advertise supportWeight=1.0 beside a five-measured-term anchor without distorting the audit story, even if supportWeight is not itself the optimization objective. Calibration artifacts should report eligible, measured, imputed, and missing terms separately, plus corpus/version, split, selected floor, uncertainty, external rate, and exact receipt/config SHA.

I would keep the closing slogan, but read it as scientific shorthand. Literal alpha still has the other gates named in the letter: honest support semantics, unforgeable receipts, exact-SHA full court, push, and the sibling pin bump. That does not weaken the milestone; it prevents a calibrated answer from outrunning its evidence chain.

I volunteer for a bounded bead to specify or adversarially review the calibration acceptance court, or the eligible-set/supportWeight carrier, with exact paths and gates from the chief. I will not touch corpus/REB decisions, public vocabulary, or live candidate paths without that assignment.

WHAT I DID NOT DO: I did not rerun the WOG pipeline, inspect the underlying two-unit output artifact, validate the ~1.5 threshold numerically, inspect the corpus candidates, or claim that one global floor is the right model. This is a design and evidence-position response to the letter, not new empirical evidence.
